name: Uganda
summary_text: Uganda is a place trans visitors should avoid entirely. The 2023 Anti-Homosexuality Act imposes life imprisonment for same-sex conduct and the death penalty for "aggravated homosexuality," and the US State Department explicitly warns that "the law applies to both visitors and residents." Over 1,000 rights violations (arrests, torture, evictions) were documented in nine months. Mobs have gathered outside trans people's homes (one woman described being grabbed and shouted at that she needed to die); police use digital entrapment (obtaining evidence via dating apps); and the government has "spread misinformation and hatred against LGBT people." The law also criminalises the "promotion of homosexuality," meaning any advocacy or support is banned. There are no laws regulating gender identity — the AHA targets same-sex conduct and promotion, not trans identity per se — but trans people are swept up in the broader anti-LGBT crackdown, mobs, and state violence. The Constitutional Court upheld the AHA in April 2024 (striking down only a few provisions on healthcare access and renting). Uganda's death penalty is for "aggravated" same-sex (not all same-sex like Iran; not gender expression per se like Saudi), and no trans-specific visitor killing or border-targeting is documented — but the systematic state-led crackdown makes this a environment to avoid entirely.

sources.title: “They’re Putting Our Lives at Risk”: How Uganda’s Anti-LGBT Climate Unleashes Abuse | HRW
sources.claim_summary: HRW report 'They're Putting Our Lives at Risk' (May 2025): how Uganda's anti-LGBT climate unleashes abuse - the 2023 Anti-Homosexuality Act (death penalty for 'aggravated homosexuality', lengthy sentences for 'promotion') has fuelled arrests, raids on shelters, evictions and public outings; many LGBT people in hiding; a small group of Ugandan mothers began speaking publicly in support of their LGBT children.

sources.title: Uganda: Court Upholds Anti-Homosexuality Act | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Apr 2024): 'Uganda: Court Upholds Anti-Homosexuality Act' — the Constitutional Court keeps the 2023 Act in force, with its life-sentence and 'aggravated' provisions intact.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (June 2024) covers rights violations against Uganda's LGBTQ community escalating, per a pressure group.

sources.title: ‘If I go out, I’ll be a target’: fear stalks Uganda over brutal anti-gay laws | LGBTQ+ rights | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Jan 2024): 'If I go out, I'll be a target' - fear stalks Uganda over brutal anti-gay laws; profiles Arianna at a safe house with 20 other transgender people on the outskirts of Kampala.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying US State Department travel advisory for Uganda includes LGBT-specific warnings under the 'Do Not Travel' advisory.

sources.title: How Uganda's anti-LGBTQ+ laws lead to entrapment
sources.claim_summary: Access Now: Uganda's anti-LGBTQ entrapment laws - analysis of how digital entrapment and surveillance are used against LGBTQ people under the Anti-Homosexuality Act framework.

sources.title: Uganda: Criminalization shrinks online civic space for LGBTQ people - report - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (Oct 2024): criminalization shrinks online civic space for LGBTQ people in Uganda - the report 'Everybody Here Is Having Two Lives or Phones' documents technology-facilitated gender-based violence (doxing, outing, threats, blackmail, impersonation, hacking, disinformation); the AHA 2023 fostered a climate of impunity, forcing individuals and organisations to alter how they engage online.

AP (Feb 2026): 'Ugandan police arrest two women for allegedly kissing in public' — two women detained in Arua after neighbours reported them; one of the first known arrests under the 2023 Anti-Homosexuality Act.

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Uganda: the three most important problems included 'violence and discrimination against marginalized groups (women...; children...; persons with disabilities; and the lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender community)' - the era of the Anti-Homosexuality Bill debates.
